articleTitle: HIFLIRTS (High Integrity data communications For Light rail Transport Systems)-digital video on train and from train to control room
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Communication Networks in Transportation
abstract: HIFLIRTS is an ERA led collaborative project supported by the DTI under the Advanced Technology Programme, Tracked Transport Initiative (TRACTS). The overall objective of HIFLIRTS is to advance the UK industry's capability in the field of data communications for light rail transport applications. The tangible outcome of the HIFLIRTS will be a laboratory demonstrator system giving a working demonstration of the results of the research and investigatory work carried out during the programme. This paper outlines the technical objectives and status of the HIFLIRTS programme. Audio and video communications from train to control room will be achieved using cellular telephone technology, and GSM has been selected as the most promising candidate.

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Communication Networks in Transportation
abstract: Nine Tiles have worked with communications networks for railway signalling, on-train information, fire detection and passenger information systems in airports and underground railways and industrial control networks. This paper briefly reviews some of the transport-related applications and discusses some of the common requirements for communications networks in this field. In the industrial field it has emerged that there are specific requirements for closely coupled control networks which are not met by currently standardised architectures. The network architectures which have been standardised so far were primarily intended for general traffic and are not always capable of providing adequate performance and resilience for time-critical applications. Therefore a task group (TCCA Group) was set up in ISO TC 184/SC5/WG2 to identify the user requirements for time-critical communications systems. Many of these requirements are directly applicable to transport systems. The TCCA report identified the communications requirements of closely coupled control systems where there was a need for bulk data transfers and time-critical messages to coexist on the same network.

articleTitle: National Motorway Communications System Mark 2-integrated highway traffic management
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Communication Networks in Transportation
abstract: The Highways Agency is committed to improving the efficiency of the existing road network and to sharing the roads investment risks with the private sector. The paper describes how the Highways Agency's National Motorway Communications System (NMCS2) can make a contribution to achieving these goals by way of its open system architecture. NMCS2 comprises an hierarchial structure of local and wide area communication networks. Within the control centre there area number of terminals known as operator interfaces (OIF). One OIF is provided for each operator and they form the focal point for the various network and traffic control facilities in the area.

articleTitle: The application of formal methods to the development of an ATP (automatic train protection) system
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Communication Networks in Transportation
abstract: We describe how the formal method communicating sequential processes (CSP) has been applied in the specification of the communication aspects of a safety-critical automatic train protection (ATP) system. We outline the requirements of such a system, and then illustrate how a theory of safety, based on the CSP notion of determinism, has been used to reason about the safety properties of such a system.
